Messages.Author: Juggernaut1981
Messages.Body:
Real life shuffling can result in clumping. If you want a completely even distribution of cards, then it isn't random.

To get your cards less clumped, then you need to turn around after a game, break them all into a small number of piles that contain the same cards in different orders and then shuffle those together. That will give you a more evenly distributed set of cards, but it is deliberately partly randomised.

Retired Baron of Sydney, Australia, 418

Messages.Author: Juggernaut1981
Messages.Body:
That's kind of my point. Random isn't shuffled. Shuffling of cards doesn't provide pure randomisation, and even distribution of cards through the deck is far from random.

Most of us want to shuffle the cards until they are effectively evenly distributed. We don't want to have them entirely randomised where we can get 8 Immortal Grapples in a row with taste of vitae for example.
